title: People's names
lead: Log the people you meet and remember their names with a technique studied for decades.
privacy: No photos, out of respect for other people's privacy. This data lives only on your device.
empty: Nobody yet. Next time you meet someone, repeat their name in the conversation and log it here.
step3Title: Build the picture in your head
name: Name
traitHint: Something you can see or hear. Pick one.
conversationHint: What you talked about: their job, a trip, their dog.
mnemonicIntro: Three steps: turn the name into something you can see, pick the most striking feature and join them in an exaggerated scene. The weirder, the better it sticks.
nameImageHint: Something concrete that sounds similar: Rose → a rose; Bill → a duck's bill; Sandy → a beach.
featureChosenHint: If it's the one you wrote before, leave it as is.
linkImageHint: Example: "a giant duck's bill bouncing off their round glasses". Picture it moving.
visualize: Close your eyes for five seconds and see this scene in detail:
visualizeAfter: If you can, say "{{name}}" out loud. We'll ask you soon, then at growing intervals.
saved: We saved {{name}}. We'll ask you their name soon.
deleteConfirm: {{name}}'s details and review card will be deleted.

quiz.title: What's their name?
quiz.wrong: You said “{{attempt}}”. You'll get it next time.
quiz.keepGoing: That's how names stick: by trying
quiz.realWorld: The real test is out there: next time you see one of these people, greet them by name.
quiz.preferWriting: I'd rather type it (the app checks it)
quiz.wrongSaid: You'll get it next time: go over your picture.

traitQuestion: What's the first thing you notice about {{name}}?
imageStep1: Think what “{{name}}” sounds like: something you can see. Rose → a rose, Bill → a duck's bill.
imageStep3: Imagine the scene exaggerated and moving. The weirder, the better it sticks.
imageExample: Example: Bill, with a beard → a giant duck's bill poking out of his beard.
imageNow: Close your eyes and look at it for a few seconds
